# Night Train: walkthrough

<!-- Generated by `npm run walkthrough` from the room manifest and its reference solutions. Do not edit by hand. -->

## Story

> Night train EN 471 "Aurora", Kleeberg to Lindholm, the night of Friday 13 November. At 02:41 the sleeping-car attendant found compartment 34 empty: the reporter Konstantin Weber is gone, his bag still on the bunk. The train is rolling on through the dark, and the federal police will board at Marienhall in half an hour.
>
> The train manager has let you into the service car. Its onboard computer logs every ticket scan, every card tap, every door and every kilometre. Find out where Weber left the train, and with whom, and radio it to the police before the train reaches Marienhall.

## Stations

### 1. The conductor's handheld

**Practises:** `LEFT JOIN` with `IS NULL`: rows that have no match  
**Needs:** 🔎 The conductor's note  
**Data:** [train.sql](../../content/rooms/sql-train/data/train.sql)

**Task:**

> Jakob Horn, the conductor, left his ticket scanner on the dining car counter. `passengers` holds the bookings, `scans` every ticket his handheld scanned tonight.
>
> Who booked a compartment but never had their ticket scanned? Show `name` and `card`.

<details><summary>Starter code</summary>

```sql
-- The tables and their columns are listed on the left. Try:
SELECT *
FROM passengers
LIMIT 5;
```

</details>

**Model solution:**

```sql
SELECT p.name, p.card
FROM passengers AS p
LEFT JOIN scans AS s ON s.ticket_id = p.ticket_id
WHERE s.scan_id IS NULL;
```

**Checked result** (rows, column names ignored, in any order):

```json
[["Hanna Vogt","C2-23"],["Paul Brenner","C5-52"]]
```

**Reveals when solved:**

> Two tickets were never scanned: **Hanna Vogt** (card `C2-23`) and **Paul Brenner** (card `C5-52`) never boarded. Compartments 23 and 52 should have stayed empty all night.

**Hints:**

1. A plain `JOIN` only keeps passengers that have a matching scan, so exactly the ones you want disappear. A `LEFT JOIN` keeps every passenger and fills the columns of `scans` with `NULL` where nothing matches.
2. `FROM passengers AS p LEFT JOIN scans AS s ON s.ticket_id = p.ticket_id`, then keep the rows without a scan: `WHERE s.scan_id IS NULL`. (`= NULL` is never true.)
3. `SELECT p.name, p.card FROM passengers AS p LEFT JOIN scans AS s ON s.ticket_id = p.ticket_id WHERE s.scan_id IS NULL;`

### 2. The speed recorder

**Practises:** `LAG() OVER (ORDER BY …)`: comparing a row with the one before; filtering a window function through a CTE  
**Needs:** 🔎 The route map  
**Data:** [train.sql](../../content/rooms/sql-train/data/train.sql)

**Task:**

> The locomotive's recorder writes down the position (`km`) and the speed (`kmh`) every two minutes.
>
> Find every halt since the train left Kleeberg: the rows where the train stands still but was still moving at the row before. Show `time` and `km`, earliest first.

<details><summary>Starter code</summary>

```sql
-- The tables and their columns are listed on the left. Try:
SELECT *
FROM speed
LIMIT 5;
```

</details>

**Model solution:**

```sql
WITH s AS (
  SELECT time, km, kmh,
         LAG(kmh) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS prev_kmh
  FROM speed
)
SELECT time, km
FROM s
WHERE kmh = 0 AND prev_kmh > 0
ORDER BY time;
```

**Checked result** (rows, column names ignored, in this order):

```json
[["2026-11-13 23:06",88],["2026-11-13 23:58",131.4],["2026-11-14 00:50",176.2],["2026-11-14 01:52",214.3]]
```

**Reveals when solved:**

> Since Kleeberg the train has halted four times: at km 88.0 (23:06), km 131.4 (23:58), km 176.2 (00:50) and km 214.3 (01:52). Only two of them are stations.

**Hints:**

1. `WHERE kmh = 0` finds every standing row, several per halt, and the building site crawls slowly without stopping. You need to compare each row with the one before it: `LAG(kmh) OVER (ORDER BY time)` gives the previous row's speed.
2. A window function can't go into `WHERE`. Compute it in a CTE first, `WITH s AS (SELECT time, km, kmh, LAG(kmh) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS prev_kmh FROM speed)`, then filter the CTE: `kmh = 0 AND prev_kmh > 0`.
3. `WITH s AS (SELECT time, km, kmh, LAG(kmh) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS prev_kmh FROM speed) SELECT time, km FROM s WHERE kmh = 0 AND prev_kmh > 0 ORDER BY time;`

### 3. The door control panel

**Practises:** `NOT EXISTS` and a correlated scalar subquery  
**Needs:** 🔎 A sign by the door panel  
**Data:** [train.sql](../../content/rooms/sql-train/data/train.sql)

**Task:**

> Every outside door reports to this panel when it opens and when it closes (`doors`). The timetable with the actual times so far is in `stations`.
>
> Which door events happened at a time when the doors should not have opened at all? Show `time`, `car`, `door`, `event` and the name of the last station the train had left before the event, earliest first.

<details><summary>Starter code</summary>

```sql
-- The tables and their columns are listed on the left. Try:
SELECT *
FROM doors
LIMIT 5;
```

</details>

**Model solution:**

```sql
SELECT d.time, d.car, d.door, d.event,
       (SELECT st.station
        FROM stations AS st
        WHERE st.departure < d.time
        ORDER BY st.departure DESC
        LIMIT 1) AS last_station
FROM doors AS d
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM stations AS s
  WHERE d.time BETWEEN s.arrival AND s.departure
)
ORDER BY d.time;
```

**Checked result** (rows, column names ignored, in this order):

```json
[["2026-11-14 01:53",3,"B","open","Felsach"],["2026-11-14 01:55",3,"B","close","Felsach"]]
```

**Reveals when solved:**

> At **01:53**, after Felsach, door B on the right of **car 3**, Konstantin Weber's car, opened on open track. It closed again at 01:55.

**Hints:**

1. The sign next to the panel says when the doors are released. For each door event, ask whether some station has the event between its `arrival` and `departure`: `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stations AS s WHERE d.time BETWEEN s.arrival AND s.departure)` keeps the events where no station does.
2. The last station left is a correlated subquery in the column list. It runs once per door event and returns one value: `(SELECT station FROM stations WHERE departure < d.time ORDER BY departure DESC LIMIT 1)`.
3. `SELECT d.time, d.car, d.door, d.event, (SELECT st.station FROM stations AS st WHERE st.departure < d.time ORDER BY st.departure DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_station FROM doors AS d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stations AS s WHERE d.time BETWEEN s.arrival AND s.departure) ORDER BY d.time;`

### 4. The card reader server

**Practises:** `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY … ORDER BY …)`: the latest row of every group  
**Needs:** 3. The door control panel (its result), 🔎 The attendant's report  
**Data:** [train.sql](../../content/rooms/sql-train/data/train.sql)

**Task:**

> Every compartment door, every washroom and every gangway door between the sleeping cars has a card reader. `taps` logs each card that was held to one.
>
> Whose card was tapped for the last time in the half hour before the door opened on open track, and never again after it? Show `card`, the `time` of its last tap and the `reader`, earliest first.

<details><summary>Starter code</summary>

```sql
-- The tables and their columns are listed on the left. Try:
SELECT *
FROM taps
LIMIT 5;
```

</details>

**Model solution:**

```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT card, time, reader,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY card ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn
  FROM taps
)
SELECT card, time, reader
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
  AND time BETWEEN '2026-11-14 01:23' AND '2026-11-14 01:53'
ORDER BY time;
```

**Checked result** (rows, column names ignored, in this order):

```json
[["C4-45","2026-11-14 01:31","door 45"],["C5-55","2026-11-14 01:41","gangway 3|4"],["C5-52","2026-11-14 01:46","gangway 3|4"],["C3-34","2026-11-14 01:49","door 34"]]
```

**Reveals when solved:**

> Four cards fall silent shortly before the door opened: `C4-45` at its own compartment door at 01:31, `C5-55` at the gangway between cars 3 and 4 at 01:41, `C5-52` at the same gangway at 01:46, and Weber's `C3-34` at his compartment door at 01:49.

**Hints:**

1. You need each card's last tap first. `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY card ORDER BY time DESC)` numbers every card's taps from the newest, so each card's last tap gets the number 1. The door's time comes from the door control panel.
2. The door opened at 01:53 on 14 November. Number the taps in a CTE, and outside it keep `rn = 1 AND time BETWEEN '2026-11-14 01:23' AND '2026-11-14 01:53'`.
3. `WITH ranked AS (SELECT card, time, reader, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY card ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn FROM taps) SELECT card, time, reader FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 AND time BETWEEN '2026-11-14 01:23' AND '2026-11-14 01:53' ORDER BY time;`

### 5. The dining car till

**Practises:** A CTE reused in a subquery (`IN (SELECT …)`), `GROUP BY` over two columns with `SUM`  
**Needs:** 1. The conductor's handheld (its result)  
**Data:** [train.sql](../../content/rooms/sql-train/data/train.sql)

**Task:**

> In the dining car, every order goes on the tab of a compartment card (`orders.card`). Whoever settles the tab pays by bank card, and the till stores the name on it as `payer`.
>
> A compartment whose passenger never boarded shouldn't have run up a bill. For the cards of those compartments, show who paid and how much in total: `card`, `payer` and the sum of `price`.

<details><summary>Starter code</summary>

```sql
-- The tables and their columns are listed on the left. Try:
SELECT *
FROM orders
LIMIT 5;
```

</details>

**Model solution:**

```sql
WITH no_shows AS (
  SELECT p.card
  FROM passengers AS p
  LEFT JOIN scans AS s ON s.ticket_id = p.ticket_id
  WHERE s.scan_id IS NULL
)
SELECT card, payer, SUM(price) AS total
FROM orders
WHERE card IN (SELECT card FROM no_shows)
GROUP BY card, payer;
```

**Checked result** (rows, column names ignored, in any order):

```json
[["C2-23","Bernd Kessler",11.4],["C5-52","Ines Hartmann",14.1],["C5-52","Konstantin Weber",7.2]]
```

**Reveals when solved:**

> Compartment 23's tab was paid by **Bernd Kessler**, compartment 52's by **Ines Hartmann**, and two hot chocolates on 52's tab by **Konstantin Weber** himself. Neither Kessler nor Hartmann has a booking.

**Hints:**

1. Which compartments' passengers never boarded is what the conductor's handheld found. Put that query into a CTE, `WITH no_shows AS (…)`, so you can use its result here.
2. Filter `orders` with `WHERE card IN (SELECT card FROM no_shows)`, then `GROUP BY card, payer` and add up with `SUM(price)`.
3. `WITH no_shows AS (SELECT p.card FROM passengers AS p LEFT JOIN scans AS s ON s.ticket_id = p.ticket_id WHERE s.scan_id IS NULL) SELECT card, payer, SUM(price) AS total FROM orders WHERE card IN (SELECT card FROM no_shows) GROUP BY card, payer;`

### 6. The train radio (Final lock)

**Practises:** Combining the results of several queries  
**Needs:** 2. The speed recorder (its result), 4. The card reader server (its result), 5. The dining car till (its result), 1. The conductor's handheld (its result), 🔒 2. The speed recorder, 🔎 The driver's log  
**Data:** [train.sql](../../content/rooms/sql-train/data/train.sql)

**Code lock** (opens with `214`):

> The radio to the police only connects once you tell it where to send them. It asks for the kilometre post, in whole kilometres, where the emergency brake stopped the train.

**Task:**

> The federal police at Marienhall answer. They are sending a patrol to the level crossing at kilometre 214 at once.
>
> One more question before the train arrives: Konstantin Weber did not leave the train alone. The police want the name of the one who left with him and was travelling in a compartment that should have stayed empty. Give the full name.
>
> You can still query the database here.

<details><summary>Starter code</summary>

```sql
-- The tables and their columns are listed on the left. Try:
SELECT *
FROM passengers
LIMIT 5;
```

</details>

**Model solution:**

```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT card, time,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY card ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn
  FROM taps
),
gone AS (
  SELECT card
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
    AND time BETWEEN '2026-11-14 01:23' AND '2026-11-14 01:53'
),
no_shows AS (
  SELECT p.card
  FROM passengers AS p
  LEFT JOIN scans AS s ON s.ticket_id = p.ticket_id
  WHERE s.scan_id IS NULL
)
SELECT DISTINCT o.card, o.payer
FROM orders AS o
WHERE o.card IN (SELECT card FROM gone)
  AND o.card IN (SELECT card FROM no_shows)
  AND o.payer NOT IN (SELECT name FROM passengers);
```

**Answer:** `Ines Hartmann`

**Hints:**

1. Besides Weber's own card, three cards fell silent just before the door in car 3 opened (card reader server). One went to bed at its own compartment door; two walked towards car 3.
2. Only one of those two cards belongs to a compartment that should have stayed empty: the conductor's handheld lists the passengers who never boarded. The other belongs to a passenger who is on board.
3. The card is `C5-52`, Paul Brenner's booking, but Brenner never boarded. The dining car till says who paid for compartment 52: Ines Hartmann, who has no booking (Weber bought hot chocolate on it too). She crossed into car 3 at 01:46 and left with him through door 3B.

## Clues in the room

### 🔎 The driver's log

*Used by: 6. The train radio*

> EN 471 AURORA · driver: P. Lanz
>
> 21:40 Kleeberg dep., on time.
> Around midnight: red signal before Ostheim, waited five minutes for a freight train.
> 00:55 Felsach dep.
> Between Felsach and Marienhall: emergency brake alarm from car 3. Stopped as the rules say. Attendant checked: handle already reset, nobody there. Continued after five minutes.

> km 152 Lindenau viaduct

### 🔎 The conductor's note

*Used by: 1. The conductor's handheld*

> A note under the handheld, in Jakob Horn's handwriting:
>
> After every station I walk the whole train and scan each ticket once. Whoever my handheld never scanned never got on. Their compartment stays locked and empty, and its card stays with the attendant.

### 🔎 A sign by the door panel

*Used by: 3. The door control panel*

> OUTSIDE DOORS
>
> The doors are released only while the train stands at a platform: from its arrival to its departure. Between stations a door opens only with the square key or the emergency release, and the panel logs it like any other.

### 🔎 The attendant's report

*Used by: 4. The card reader server*

> Pinned to the door of compartment 34. Mira Szabo, sleeping-car attendant, 02:41:
>
> Compartment 34 empty. Bed not slept in, bag on the bunk, coat and shoes gone. Mr Weber's card is not in the compartment.
>
> At night the gangway doors between the sleeping cars are locked. They open with any compartment card or a staff card (`S-…`), and the reader logs who passed.

### 🔎 A newspaper

*Used by: flavour only*

> KLEEBERG DAILY · Friday, 13 November 2026
>
> THE MISSING MILLIONS OF THE NEW BRIDGE: reporter Konstantin Weber to testify in Lindholm on Monday. Weber says he has received threats and "will not travel the way people expect".

## Handbook in the room: 📖 The onboard computer's binder

**Rows without a match:** [`a LEFT JOIN b ON …`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_select.html#fromclause), [`x IS NULL / x IS NOT NULL`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#isisnot)

**Subqueries:** [`x IN (SELECT …)`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#in_op), [`EXISTS (SELECT …)`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#exists_op), [`(SELECT … LIMIT 1)`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#subq), [`correlated subquery`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#cosub)

**Common table expressions:** [`WITH name AS (SELECT …) SELECT … FROM name`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_with.html#ordinarycte)

**Window functions:** [`f(…) OVER (ORDER BY col)`](https://www.sqlite.org/windowfunctions.html), [`OVER (PARTITION BY col ORDER BY …)`](https://www.sqlite.org/windowfunctions.html#ptxn), [`LAG(col) / LEAD(col)`](https://www.sqlite.org/windowfunctions.html#biwinfunc), [`ROW_NUMBER()`](https://www.sqlite.org/windowfunctions.html#biwinfunc), [`filtering by a window function`](https://www.sqlite.org/windowfunctions.html)

**Adding up and times:** [`SUM(col)`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_aggfunc.html#sumunc), [`'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'`](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_datefunc.html)
